paragraphs: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation is a financial holding company and bank holding company organized under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia and registered under the BHCA. We are headquartered in Richmond, Virginia and provide a wide range of financial services and products to commercial and retail clients through our wholly owned subsidiary bank, Atlantic Union Bank, a Federal Reserve member bank charted under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia.

The Bank is headquartered in Richmond, Virginia and operates branches and ATMs located in Virginia, Maryland, Washington, D.C., and North Carolina. In addition, our non-bank financial services affiliates include Atlantic Union Equipment Finance, Inc., which provides equipment financing; AUB Investments, Inc., which provides investment services; and Atlantic Union Capital Markets, Inc., which provides capital market services.
At December 31, 2025, we had $37.6 billion in assets, $27.8 billion in LHFI, $30.5 billion in deposits, and $5.0 billion in stockholders' equity.
Acquisition of Sandy Spring Bancorp, Inc.

On April 1, 2025, we completed our merger with Sandy Spring, the bank holding company for Sandy Spring Bank, and we successfully completed the integration of Sandy Spring branches and operations on October 14, 2025. With the acquisition of Sandy Spring, we acquired more than 50 branches in Virginia, Maryland, and Washington, D.C., enhancing our presence in Northern Virginia and Maryland.

On June 26, 2025, we completed the sale of performing CRE loans acquired in the Sandy Spring acquisition with an unpaid principal balance of $2.0 billion, which we marked to fair value at $1.8 billion and classified as held for sale as of the April 1, 2025 acquisition date. The CRE loan sale transaction generated a $10.9 million pre-tax gain, net of transaction expenses, for the year ended 2025. Under the terms of the loan purchase agreement, we sold the loans without recourse and retained customer-facing servicing responsibilities.

On October 21, 2024, in connection with the execution of the Sandy Spring merger agreement, we entered into an initial forward sale agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC (the "Forward Purchaser") relating to an aggregate of 9,859,155 shares of our common stock. On October 21, 2024, we priced the public offering of shares of our common stock in connection with such forward sale agreement and entered into an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representative for the underwriters named therein, the Forward Purchaser and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC as forward seller (the "Forward Seller"), relating to the registered public offering and sale of 9,859,155 shares of our common stock at a public offering price of $35.50 per share (before underwriting discounts and commissions). The underwriters were granted a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1,478,873 shares of our common stock. On October 21, 2024, the underwriters exercised in full their option to purchase the additional 1,478,873 shares of our common stock pursuant to the underwriting agreement and, in connection therewith, we entered into an additional forward sale agreement with the Forward Purchaser relating to 1,478,873 shares of our common stock, on terms substantially similar to those contained in the initial forward sale agreement (such additional forward sale agreement together with the initial forward sale agreement, the "Forward Sale Agreements").

On April 1, 2025, we physically settled in full the Forward Sale Agreements by delivering 11,338,028 shares of our common stock to the Forward Purchaser. We received net proceeds from such sale of shares of our common stock and full physical settlement of the Forward Sale Agreements, before expenses, of approximately $385.0 million.

The Company was originally incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia in 1991, and we completed our bank holding company formation in July 1993, in connection with the merger of Northern Neck Bankshares Corporation with and into Union Bancorp, Inc. to form Union Bankshares Corporation, which was renamed Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation in 2019.

Union Bank & Trust Company, a predecessor of Atlantic Union Bank, was formed in 1902, and certain other of the community banks that were acquired and ultimately merged to form what is now Atlantic Union Bank were among the oldest in Virginia at the time they were acquired.

We have a history of growing through both organic growth and strategic acquisitions, particularly with our five most recent acquisitions—StellarOne Corporation in 2014, Xenith Bankshares, Inc. in 2018, Access National Corporation in 2019, American National in 2024, and Sandy Spring in 2025—which allowed us to meaningfully increase our asset size, enhance our scale and expand our footprint in Virginia, Maryland, Washington, D.C., and North Carolina.

headings: Risks Related to Our Lending Activities
Our ACL may prove to be insufficient to absorb credit losses in our loan portfolio, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
A significant portion of our loan portfolio is secured by real estate and events that negatively impact the real estate market could hurt our business.
We have significant credit exposure in CRE, which may expose us to additional credit risks, and may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our loan portfolio contains construction and development loans, which may expose us to additional credit risks, and may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

Our commercial and industrial loans are a significant component of our loan portfolio, which may expose us to additional credit risks, and may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
The loans we make through federal programs are dependent on the federal government's continuation and support of these programs and on our compliance with program requirements.

We use independent appraisals and other valuation techniques in evaluating and monitoring loans secured by real estate and other real estate owned, which may not accurately describe the net value of the asset.
If we fail to effectively manage credit risk, our business and financial condition will suffer.
Our lending to small to mid-sized community-based businesses may increase our credit risk.
Nonperforming assets take significant time to resolve and may adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

Our mortgage revenue is cyclical and sensitive to interest rates, changes in economic conditions, decreased economic activity, and slowdowns in the housing market, any of which could adversely impact our profits.
We may be required to repurchase mortgage loans or indemnify buyers against losses in some circumstances, which could harm our liquidity, results of operations and financial condition.
We are subject to environmental risks.
Risks Related to Our Business, Industry, Markets, and Market Interest Rates
We may not be able to maintain a strong core deposit base or access other low-cost funding sources
We face substantial competition that could adversely affect our growth and/or operating results.
Consumers may increasingly decide not to use banks to complete their financial transactions, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Changes in interest rates could adversely affect our income and cash flows.
We may incur losses if asset values decline, including due to changes in interest rates and prepayment speeds.
Our business strategy includes continued growth, and our financial condition and results of operation could be negatively affected if we fail to grow or fail to manage our growth effectively.
We may be adversely affected by risks associated with future mergers and acquisition, including execution risk which could disrupt our business and dilute shareholder value.
The carrying value of goodwill and other intangible assets may be adversely affected.
Our risk-management framework may not be effective in mitigating risks and/or losses.
We use models in our business, and we could be adversely affected if our design, implementation, or use of models is flawed.
paragraphs: An investment in our securities involves risks and uncertainties. In addition to the other information set forth in this Form 10-K, including the information addressed under "Forward-Looking Statements," investors in our securities should carefully consider the risk factors discussed below. These factors could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations, and capital position and could cause our actual results to differ materially from our historical results or the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this Form 10-K, in which case the trading price of our securities could decline. The risk factors discussed below highlight the risks that we believe are material to us, but do not necessarily include all risks that we may face, and an investor in our securities should not interpret the disclosure of a risk in the following risk factors to state or imply that the risk has not already materialized.

Our success depends significantly on the quality of our assets, particularly loans. Like all financial institutions, we are exposed to the risk that our borrowers may not repay their loans according to their terms, and the collateral securing the payment of these loans may be insufficient to fully compensate us for the outstanding balance of the loan plus the costs to dispose of the collateral.

We maintain an ACL, which includes the ALLL, at a level we believe is adequate to absorb expected losses in our loan portfolio as of the corresponding balance sheet date. The process to determine the ACL uses models and assumptions that require us to make difficult and complex judgments that are often interrelated. This includes forecasting how borrowers will perform in changing and unprecedented economic conditions. The ability of our borrowers to repay their obligations will likely be impacted by changes in future economic conditions, which in turn could impact the accuracy of our loss forecasts and allowance estimates. There is also the possibility that we have failed or will fail to accurately identify the appropriate economic indicators, to accurately estimate the timing of future changes in economic conditions, or to estimate accurately the impacts of future changes in economic conditions to our borrowers, which similarly could impact the accuracy of our loss forecasts and allowance estimates.

If the models, estimates, and assumptions we use to establish reserves or the judgments we make in extending credit to our borrowers prove inaccurate in predicting future events, we may suffer unexpected losses. The ACL is our best estimate of expected credit losses; however, there is no guarantee that it will be sufficient to address credit losses, particularly if the economic outlook deteriorates significantly and quickly. In such an event, we may increase our ACL, which would reduce our earnings and capital. Additionally, to the extent that economic conditions worsen, impacting our consumer and commercial borrowers or underlying collateral, and credit losses are worse than expected, as may be caused by inflation, an economic recession or otherwise, we may increase our provision for loan losses, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

A significant portion of our loan portfolio is secured by real estate located in our core banking markets. The real estate collateral in each case provides an alternate source of repayment in the event of default by the borrower and may deteriorate in value during the time the credit is extended. A decline in local economic conditions may have a greater effect on our earnings and capital than on the earnings and capital of other financial institutions whose real estate loan portfolios are more geographically diverse. Deterioration in national real estate market conditions, or in conditions in specific local real estate markets, could cause us to adjust our opinion of the level of credit quality in our loan portfolio. Such a determination may lead to an additional increase in our ACL, which could also adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Additionally, changes in the real estate market could also affect the value of foreclosed assets, which could cause additional losses when management determines it is appropriate to sell the assets.

Our CRE portfolio consists primarily of non-owner-operated properties and other commercial properties. These types of loans are generally viewed as having more risk of default than residential real estate loans and depend on cash flows from the owner's business or the property's tenants to service the debt. The borrower's cash flows may be affected significantly by general economic conditions, a downturn in the local economy or in occupancy rates in the market where the property is located, any of which could increase the likelihood of default. CRE loans also typically have larger loan balances, and, therefore, the deterioration of one or a few of these loans could cause a significant increase in the percentage of our non-performing loans. An increase in non-performing loans could result in a loss of earnings from these loans, an increase in the provision for loan losses, and an increase in charge-offs, all of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

paragraphs: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation 為一間財務控股公司及銀行控股公司，依維吉尼亞州法律設立，並已註冊於 BHCA。本公司總部設於維吉尼亞州里士滿市，透過我們的 wholly owned subsidiary bank，Atlantic Union Bank，一間屬於聯邦儲備銀行會員的銀行，依照維吉尼亞州法律設立，為商業與零售客戶提供廣泛的財務服務與產品。
該銀行總部設於維吉尼亞州里士滿市，並在維吉尼亞州、馬裏蘭州、華盛頓特區與北卡羅萊納州設有分行與 ATM。此外，我們的非銀行財務服務子公司包括 Atlantic Union Equipment Finance, Inc.，提供設備融資服務；AUB Investments, Inc.，提供投資服務；以及 Atlantic Union Capital Markets, Inc.，提供資本市場服務。
於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司資產為 376 億美元，LHFI 為 278 億美元，存款為 305 億美元，股東權益為 50 億美元。
收購 Sandy Spring Bancorp, Inc.
於 2025 年 4 月 1 日，我們完成與 Sandy Spring 的合併，Sandy Spring 為 Sandy Spring Bank 的銀行控股公司，並於 2025 年 10 月 14 日成功整合 Sandy Spring 的分行與營運。透過收購 Sandy Spring，我們取得超過 50 家分行，位於維吉尼亞州、馬裏蘭州與華盛頓特區，強化我們在北部維吉尼亞州與馬裏蘭州的經營據點。

於 2025 年 6 月 26 日，我們完成出售於 Sandy Spring 收購中取得之 performing CRE 按揭貸款，該貸款未償本金餘額為 2.0 十億美元，我們以公平價值 1.8 十億美元標記，並於 2025 年 4 月 1 日收購日歸類為持有待售。該 CRE 按揭貸款出售交易於 2025 年度產生稅前獲利 10.9 百萬美元，扣除交易費用後淨額。根據貸款購買協議條款，我們無追索權出售貸款，並保留面對客戶的服務責任。

於 2024 年 10 月 21 日，根據執行 Sandy Spring 合併協議，我們與 Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC（"Forward Purchaser"）簽訂一項初始遠期銷售協議，涉及我們 9,859,155 股普通股。於 2024 年 10 月 21 日，我們根據該遠期銷售協議，進行普通股公開發行，並與 Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC 簽訂承銷協議，作為承銷商代表，Forward Purchaser 以及 Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC 作為遠期賣方（"Forward Seller"），涉及註冊公開發行與銷售 9,859,155 股普通股，每股公開發行價格為 35.50 美元（扣除承銷折扣與佣金前）。承銷商獲得了 30 天的選擇權，可購買最多 1,478,873 股普通股。於 2024 年 10 月 21 日，承銷商已完全行使其選擇權，購買額外的 1,478,873 股普通股，根據承銷協議，我們與 Forward Purchaser 簽訂一項額外遠期銷售協議，涉及 1,478,873 股普通股，條款與初始遠期銷售協議 substantially similar（此額外遠期銷售協議與初始遠期銷售協議合稱為 "Forward Sale Agreements"）。
於 2025 年 4 月 1 日，我們透過交付 11,338,028  shares 本公司普通股，實際履行 Forward Sale Agreements 全額結算。我們自該出售本公司普通股及 Forward Sale Agreements 全額實質結算，扣除費用前，約收到 385.0 百萬美元淨現金。
本公司最初於維吉尼亞州法律下設立，時間為1991年，我們於1993年7月完成銀行控股公司設立，與Northern Neck Bankshares Corporation與Union Bancorp, Inc.合併，成立Union Bankshares Corporation，後於2019年更名為Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation。
Union Bank & Trust Company，為Atlantic Union Bank之前身，於1902年成立，且某些其他被收購並最終合併成為現今Atlantic Union Bank之社區銀行，在被收購時為維吉尼亞州最古老的銀行之一。

我們有透過內生成長與戰略收購來擴張的歷史，特別是我們最近的五次收購—StellarOne Corporation於2014年、Xenith Bankshares, Inc.於2018年、Access National Corporation於2019年、American National於2024年，以及Sandy Spring於2025年—使我們得以顯著增加資產規模，提升規模效益，並擴大在維吉尼亞州、馬裏蘭州、華盛頓特區與北卡羅來納州的業務版圖。

headings: 與我們貸款業務相關的風險
我們的應計貸款減損可能無法足夠吸收貸款組閤中的信用減損，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們貸款組合的很大一部分是以不動產為擔保，而對不動產市場產生負面影響的事件可能會傷害我們的業務。
我們在商業不動產領域有顯著的信用風險敞口，這可能會使我們面臨額外的信用風險，並可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們的貸款組合包含建設及開發貸款，這可能會使我們面臨額外的信用風險，並可能對我們的營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們的商業及工業貸款是我們貸款組合的重要零組件，這可能會使我們面臨額外的信用風險，並可能對我們的營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們透過聯邦計畫所發放的貸款取決於聯邦政府持續並支持這些計畫，以及我們符合計畫要求的情況。
我們在評估及監控以不動產為擔保或擁有其他不動產的貸款時，會使用獨立評估及其它估值技術，這些技術可能無法準確反映資產的淨價值。
若我們未能有效管理信用風險，將會影響我們的業務與財務狀況。
我們對中小型社區企業的貸款可能增加我們的信用風險。
不良資產需要相當長的時間才能解決，並可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們的房貸收入具有週期性，且對利率、經濟條件變動、經濟活動減少及房屋市場放緩等因素敏感，任何一種情況都可能對我們的利潤產生不利影響。
在某些情況下，我們可能被要求回購房貸貸款或賠償買方的損失，這可能會損害我們的流動性、營運結果與財務狀況。
與我們的業務、產業、市場及市場利率相關的風險
我們可能無法維持強勁的核心存款基礎或取得其他低成本資金來源
我們面臨著龐大的競爭，這可能會對我們的成長及/或營運結果產生不利影響。
消費者可能越來越決定不透過銀行完成其財務交易，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
利率的變動可能會對我們的收入及現金流產生不利影響。
如果資產價值下跌，我們可能會產生虧損，包括因利率變動及預先償還速度變動所致。
與我們營運相關的風險
我們的業務策略包括持續成長，若我們未能成長或未能有效管理成長，可能會對我們的財務狀況及營運結果產生負面影響。
我們可能因未來合併及收購相關的風險而受到不利影響，包括執行風險，這可能會干擾我們的業務並稀釋股東價值。
商譽及其他無形資產的帳面價值可能會受到不利影響。
本公司風險管理架構可能無法有效降低風險及/或損失。
我們在業務中使用模型，若我們的模型設計、實作或使用有瑕疵，可能會對我們造成不利影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及風險與不確定性。除本 Form 10-K 所載之其他資訊，包括「前瞻性陳述」部分所述資訊外，投資人應謹慎考量下列風險因素。這些因素可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運成果及資本地位造成重大且不利的影響，並可能使本公司實際結果與歷史結果或本 Form 10-K 所含前瞻性陳述所預期結果產生重大差異，進而使本公司證券交易價格下跌。下列風險因素強調本公司認為對本公司重要的風險，但未必包含本公司可能面臨的所有風險，投資人不得將下列風險因素中披露之風險視為已實現或未實現。
本公司之成功在很大程度上取決於資產品質，尤其是貸款。如同所有金融機構，本公司面臨借款人未能依照貸款條款償還貸款之風險，且用以擔保貸款償付之抵押品可能不足以完全補償貸款餘額及處置抵押品之成本。

本公司維持一個 ACL，包含 ALLL，於我們認為足以吸收貸款組合截至對應資產負債表日期預期損失之水準。確定 ACL 之程序使用模型與假設，需要我們做出困難且複雜之判斷，這些判斷往往相互關聯。這包括預測借款人在變動且前所未有的經濟條件下之表現。借款人償還義務之能力很可能受到未來經濟條件變化的影響，進而影響我們損失預測與撥備估計之準確性。此外，也有可能我們未能正確識別適當之經濟指標，或未能正確估計未來經濟條件變化的時間點，或未能正確估計未來經濟條件變化對借款人之影響，這也會影響我們損失預測與撥備估計之準確性。

若我們用以建立撥備之模型、估計與假設，或在對借款人授信時所做出之判斷，未能準確預測未來事件，我們可能遭受預期之外之損失。ACL 是我們對預期信用損失之最佳估計；然而，無法保證其足夠應對信用損失，特別是在經濟展望顯著且迅速惡化的情況下。在這種情況下，我們可能提高 ACL，這將降低我們之獲利與資本。此外，若經濟條件惡化，影響我們之消費者與商業借款人或其背後抵押品，且信用損失高於預期，如可能由通貨膨脹、經濟衰退或其他因素造成，我們可能提高貸款損失撥備，這可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。

本公司貸款組閤中相當一部分由位於我們核心銀行營運地區之不動產擔保。每筆貸款之不動產抵押品在借款人違約時提供替代償還來源，且在信用延長期間抵押品價值可能下降。地方經濟條件惡化可能對本公司獲利與資本之影響，可能大於其他金融機構之影響，因其不動產貸款組合地理分佈較為多元。國家或特定地方不動產市場條件惡化，可能導致我們調整對貸款組合信用品質之看法。此種判斷可能導致我們進一步提高 ACL，這也可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。此外，不動產市場之變化也可能影響被沒收資產之價值，當管理層認為適當時出售資產，可能導致額外損失。

本公司之商業不動產貸款組合主要由非自有經營之不動產及其他商業不動產組成。這些類型貸款通常被視為較住宅不動產貸款有更高違約風險，且依賴所有者業務或不動產租戶之現金流以償還債務。借款人之現金流可能受到總體經濟條件、地方經濟衰退或市場中不動產佔用率變動之顯著影響，任何一種情況都可能增加違約可能性。商業不動產貸款通常貸款金額較高，因此，其中一筆或幾筆貸款惡化可能導致本公司非 Performing 貸款佔比顯著上升。非 Performing 貸款增加可能導致來自這些貸款之獲利減少、貸款損失撥備增加及帳面損失增加，所有這些都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
